messages:
Lia: FYI support ticket from CustGreen — reports p99 API latency ~700-900ms from APAC to eu-west started ~07:40 UTC. They see a lot of TLS early-close and occasional auth timeouts. Anyone on call? :rotating_light:
Alex: seeing it in our apac->eu synthetic probe mesh too. Spike started ~07:38 UTC. p95 ~120ms but p99 jumps. Traceroute looks weird, extra hop through us-west for some paths.
Jordan: link to probe dashboard: https://dash/redwood/probes?probe=apac-eu&from=07:00&to=08:30
Sam: ran a quick dig trace from apac-pop-3: `dig +trace api-cust.redwood.example` — got an extra CNAME and then TTLs flipping on second A lookup. Suspect GSLB change.
Alex: sharing traceroute snippet from apac-pop-3 -> eu-west at 07:42:
```
traceroute to api-cust (34.120.5.6), 30 hops max
 1  10.1.0.1 (10.1.0.1)  0.48 ms
 2  100.64.2.1 (100.64.2.1)  1.2 ms
 3  203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45)  6.8 ms
 4  198.51.100.9 (198.51.100.9)  130.5 ms  <-- unexpected hop (us-west)
 5  34.120.5.6 (34.120.5.6)  140.1 ms
```
Lia: that extra hop lines up with the p99 increases. Also saw TLS alerts in the logs: `TLS alert 40 (handshake_failure)` then `unexpected eof` on server side.
Jordan: checking BGP announcements — slight community change propagated from partner peer at 07:35 per bgp-monitor. Looks like a prepending got removed causing some prefixes to prefer a path via partner that hairpins through us-west.
Sam: pinned down auth errors to token exchange retries after TLS early close. Client retries increase latency to p99.
Alex: quick mitigation idea: force egress affinity for apac-pop-3 to prefer local eu-west POP by setting GSLB weight override for custgreen prefixes. Can we do a temporary override?
Lia: +1 do it. Sam, can you prepare the override? Jordan, do we need router-level prepends rolled back?
Jordan: we can push a GSLB weight override immediately. Router-prepend rollback needs change window, prefer the GSLB override for fast mitigation.
Sam: applying weight override now for custgreen zone -> target eu-west (command):
```
curl -X POST https://gslb-api.local/override \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"zone":"custgreen","region":"eu-west","weight":100,"ttl":30}'
```
deploy-bot: GSLB override request accepted (id: ov-2026-07). Propagating to POPs.
Alex: probes show p99 falling already in apac-pop-3 — down from ~850ms to ~140ms at 07:52 UTC. 
Lia: Support notified CustGreen of a temporary routing override and asked them to verify.
support-bot: CustGreen confirmed improved latency and auth requests succeed. Thanks! :white_check_mark:
Jordan: root cause summary so far: partner BGP change removed a prepending that had been keeping traffic off their transit path. That resulted in an anycast/GSLB decision that caused some APAC egresses to route via partner transit through us-west, adding RTT and causing TLS sessions to tear (likely due to MTU path or mid-connection NAT).
Sam: follow-ups: 1) rollback partner prepending change or coordinate with partner; 2) add guardrail to GSLB to avoid sudden weight flips when upstream AS changes; 3) add synthetic path-diff alert for APAC->EU that triggers on hop-count or RTT delta > 50ms at p99.
Lia: + add a short-term retention on TLS alert logs for impacted prefixes and capture PCAP if it happens again. Also postmortem to eng-ops and cust-success.
Alex: creating incident ticket and assigning postmortem owners. Incident ID I-2026-437.
Jordan: I'll open a follow-up with partner ops to restore the intended prepends and ask for confirmation of no further announcements.
Lia: thanks team. Marking this thread resolved for now, will update with postmortem link. :v:
